about.html:
About this site

The theorem. J.H. Conway, An enumeration of knots and links, and some of their algebraic properties (1970): two rational tangles are isotopic if and only if they have the same fraction. The proof followed here is Louis H. Kauffman and Sofia Lambropoulou, On the classification of rational tangles, Adv. Appl. Math. 33 (2004) 199–237 (arXiv:math/0311499). It computes the fraction by integer colorings of the arcs.

The Lean. tangentproofs/conway-knots: about 26,000 lines of Lean 4 on Mathlib (v4.32.2) in 32 files, by Michal Wallace, developed with AutoformBot. The project's own blueprint is the project home.

What it proves, in one paragraph. Tangles are given as twist recipes (one crossing glued on at a time). If two top-product-free recipes have the same fraction, their diagrams are isotopic. That is the reconstruction half, proved through the unique canonical continued fraction. Every non-constant integer coloring of a (slideReady) twist diagram reads off the fraction (f = F). Fractions and coloring fractions are unchanged along a restricted, one-way set of moves (ColoringIsotopy). Conway's theorem itself is not proved: the two halves are about different move sets and don't combine into an "if and only if". See the review.

This site reads the formal statements back into plain English, so you can judge whether they say what their names suggest. Each node is one Lean declaration with its verbatim Lean, a plain-English reading that leads with its most surprising point, faithfulness notes, and a short quiz. Tick I think I understand this when you do. The four headline theorems have step-by-step proof outlines linked to their exact lines.

The Lean source is on the site, highlighted. Names defined in the project link to their definitions, Mathlib names link to the Mathlib docs, and every "File.lean lines a–b" reference opens those exact lines.

Start with the statements, then read the review and what was and wasn't checked.

Proof outlines and quizzes are summaries, not evidence: the Lean is the ground truth.

Credit. Theorem: J.H. Conway; proof followed: Kauffman and Lambropoulou. Lean: Michal Wallace with AutoformBot. Explanations: drafts by Grok Bot for Michal Wallace (review: draft), possibly wrong. Site engine: the tangentproofs proof-site kit (star-height, subexponential-sat).

review.html:
The review: do the statements say what the names say?

Each headline was read against Kauffman–Lambropoulou by Grok Bot. It was then audited independently by Claude from the source alone (no build). The full audit is committed as learn/CLAUDE_AUDIT.md, and its findings are applied to the node pages.

Headline Classical claim Verdict
rational_classification_fragment Theorem 1 (Conway): isotopic ⇔ same fraction PARTIAL. Not an iff. Both conclusions follow from a ColoringIsotopy hypothesis, and the "isotopic" conclusion nearly follows from that hypothesis directly. Top-product-free, slideReady recipes only.
twist_same_fraction_isotopic_of_noMulTop Theorem 3: same fraction ⇒ isotopic Faithful with caveats. Real content and every fraction covered, but about recipes, not tangles. It concludes the repo's Isotopic, with assumed moves, and depends on native_decide.
coloring_fraction_invariant_ColoringIsotopy Theorem 2: the fraction is an isotopy invariant PARTIAL. Invariance along a smaller, one-way set of moves. Flype slides, half-turns, mirror and inversion moves and transfer moves are excluded.
coloring_fraction_eq_F_any_slideReady Theorem 4: f = F Faithful with caveats. Every non-constant coloring of a slideReady twist diagram reads off the standard-form fraction. It is about twist diagrams, not arbitrary rational diagrams.

What a careful reader should know

  1. The halves don't meet. Invariance is proved along ColoringIsotopy; reconstruction concludes Isotopic, a larger relation. No "iff" follows for either.
  2. The recipe fraction has a slip on top products. TwistExpr.fraction computes 1/(s + F) for a top product, where the Conway product needs 1/(s + 1/F). They agree only when F = ±1. Example: [+1] * [0] isotopes to [0] (fraction 0), but the formula gives 1. The classification headlines assume noMulTop, where the formula is right, and the coloring headlines use the standard-form fraction instead. So the headlines are unaffected, but noMulTop is load-bearing for what they mean.
  3. Isotopic is a list of assumed moves. Beyond Reidemeister moves, it takes flypes, half-turns, inversion identities and the Figure 14 transfer moves as generators. The flype slide is stated with a half-turn (two flips) of an arbitrary sub-diagram. The classical flype uses one flip, and the two agree on rational pieces but maybe not in general. Every use I found is on a rational piece. If Isotopic were too generous, "same fraction ⇒ isotopic" would be weaker, not false.
  4. Refuted shortcuts, not refuted moves. not_coloring_mirror_transport and not_coloring_invert_transport show that a coloring can't always be carried from a diagram to its mirror or inverse with the same boundary colors. This rules out the simplest way of extending the coloring proof to those moves. It doesn't show any move is wrong.
  5. The excluded port cases are real. slideReady rules out gluing a crossing onto a bare strand (left of [∞], top of [0]). There the diagonal rule fails, and the repo proves it (not_diagonal_addLeft_infinity, not_diagonal_mulTop_zero).
  6. The docstrings are candid. For example: "Full Isotopic invariance in either direction is not claimed: the excluded generators are unproved". The audit found nothing dressed up as more than it is.
  7. Nothing was built, and two headlines depend on native_decide. See Trust.

Smuggled hypotheses?

None found. noMulTop and slideReady are visible restrictions, and the audit argues they are essential (one for meaning, one for truth). The one hypothesis that does heavy lifting is ColoringIsotopy in headline 1, and it is stated plainly in the signature.

Wording the audit would not allow

"Conway's theorem formalized", "rational tangles are classified by their fraction, verified in Lean", "the fraction is an isotopy invariant" without naming ColoringIsotopy, and "zero sorries, fully verified".

trust.html:
Trust: what has and hasn't been checked

This site explains the Lean. It does not re-check it.

Lean checking

main @ 76792ca (Lean files last changed in 76792ca, 2026-09-08)
Built by this site no. By the owner's choice, no Lean was built on our servers for this site.
Built publicly (CI) no Lean CI in the repository. The README says Lean is not installed in its workspace and asks not to run lake build until a toolchain is available.
#print axioms not run. No output is recorded in the repository.
sorry, admit, axiom none found by grep in src/
implemented_by, extern, unsafe none found by grep
native_decide 6 uses, all in ContinuedFractionFormExists.lean (lines 32, 37, 353, 358, 363, 368). They check small PD-code computations: the R2 cancellation [+1] + [−1] → [0] and the R1 kinks [∞] + [±1] → [∞]. native_decide trusts the compiler, not the kernel (axiom Lean.ofReduceBool).
Which headlines reach them By the source scan and the Claude audit: twist_same_fraction_isotopic_of_noMulTop and so rational_classification_fragment. Probably not coloring_fraction_invariant_ColoringIsotopy or coloring_fraction_eq_F_any_slideReady. Only #print axioms after a build can confirm this.
Small decide many, on small PD-code / Fin goals: ordinary kernel checking
Dependencies Mathlib only

The six native_decide goals are one- and two-crossing code equalities. They look replaceable by decide or rfl, which would remove the exposure.

What the Lean does not contain

  • Conway's theorem. There is no statement "isotopic ⇔ same fraction". The source's own header (RationalTangles.lean) says: "The classification theorem is not yet stated."
  • Invariance under full isotopy. The fraction is proved invariant only along ColoringIsotopy, a smaller one-way relation. It isn't proved invariant along Isotopic.
  • A fraction for a tangle. Fractions belong to twist recipes. "The fraction of a rational tangle up to isotopy" is not defined.
  • Top products. Recipes with mulTop are excluded from the classification headlines, and there the recipe fraction TwistExpr.fraction is not the Conway fraction.
  • Isotopy from first principles. Isotopic takes flypes, half-turns, inversion identities and the transfer moves as primitive generators. One generator, flype_slide_add/mul, may be stronger than real isotopy for non-rational pieces (Claude audit, §5).
  • Well-formedness and planarity. TangleDiagram has no planarity condition. WellFormed is a hypothesis of two ColoringIsotopy moves and is proved for nothing.

This site's own data

  • Declarations were read from the source text, not a Lean build. learn/tools/scan_decls.py finds every top-level declaration (1760) with its exact lines and text, and every declaration carries "extracted": false. "Mentions" and "proof uses" edges are matched by name, including x.method and (f x).method calls resolved from binder and return types. They may miss or misattribute a few uses.
  • Identifier links on the source pages come from the same name matching (data/xref.json is marked "heuristic": true). Names under core and Mathlib namespaces (List., Nat., Int., Rat., …) link to the Mathlib docs search.
  • Audit. The headline statements were audited by a second model (Claude), reading the source only; see the review and learn/CLAUDE_AUDIT.md.
  • Explanations are drafts by Grok Bot (review: draft), not yet checked by a human.

To upgrade this page

Build on a capable machine (lake exe cache get && lake build), run #print axioms for each headline, replace scan_decls.py with ExtractDecls.lean + build_xref.py as on the other tangentproofs sites, and replace the "no" entries above.
